newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Sept qtr GDP growth higher than forecast.
newsitem.headline: NZ Sept qtr GDP growth higher than forecast.

text.p: New Zealand economic growth in the September 1996 quarter was stronger than economists had expected, with a real seasonally adjusted rise in gross domestic product of 0.6 percent, Statistics NZ said on Thursday.
A survey of 13 economists by Reuters expected growth in the quarter to be 0.21 percent.
Government Statistican Len Cook said the economy continued to slow following the relatively strong growth during 1994 and 1995.
Cook said business investment remained at high levels, up 8.3 percent for the September year, although this was lower than the 14.2 percent annual increase recorded in September 1995.
Business activity, which excludes general government and owner-occupied housing grew 1.2 percent in the September quarter.

Service industry growth was a consistent 1.3 percent for the quarter and 4.3 percent for the year. All services grew except wholesale and retail trade. Manufacturing was up 1.9 percent for the quarter after falling in June.But much of the increased production had entered stocks, Cook said.

The recovery in manufacturing was strong enough to offset further falls in energy and construction industries. Annual growth in manufacturing was 0.8 percent for the September year, down from 5.7 percent the previous year.
Primary industry production rose 1.3 percent despite a 1.3 percent fall in agriculture and a decline in fishing. Strong growth in forestry and oil and gas extraction contributed to the overall rise.
The expenditure-based measure of GDP increased 0.9 percent for the September 1996 quarter after a 0.1 percent rise in the June quarter.
The GDP implicit price deflator, a broad measure of overall price changes for final goods and services, increased by 2.1 percent in the September 1996 year.
